Ongoing terrors resemble that of 1971 war
2015-02-28T01:05:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/city/ongoing-terrors-resemble-1971-war-4302

Foreign Minister Abul Hassan Mahmood Ali yesterday said the ongoing indiscriminate acts of violence, arson and terror being perpetrated by the BNP-Jamaat-e-Islami combine has a stark resemblance to the atrocities people witnessed in 1971 during the Liberation War.

In the last four decades after the country's independence, such forces gathered within democratic spaces and resorted to terrorist acts under the pretext of political movement, he said.

Mahmood was addressing the inaugural ceremony of a three-day "International Conference on Bangladesh Genocide and Justice" organised by Liberation War Museum in the capital's Cirdap auditorium.

He urged conscious citizen of the world to reject such violent acts of terror.

There can be no meaningful engagement with quarters that support and believe in terrorism to substantiate their political agenda, he added.

UN Special Adviser for the Prevention of Genocide and Responsibility to Protect Adama Dieng, in a video message, said the massacres, rape, acts of torture, disappearances, displacements and destruction and confiscation of property during in 1971 were crimes that should not be forgotten.

"...undertaking judicial process particularly related to the prosecution of atrocity crimes has important results that are linked to prevention. This includes the deterrence of future crimes, the strengthening of the reconciliation process and the maintenance of peace and security," he said.

In the plenary session, Barrister Tureen Afroz compared Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunals with others around the world, pointing out that here there were instances that bail was granted and the provision of filing review petitions with the apex court existed.
